claims.text: Instant messenger use is positively related to compulsive Internet use six months later in adolescents.
Chatting in chat rooms is positively related to compulsive Internet use six months later in adolescents.
Instant messenger use is positively associated with depression six months later in adolescents.
Loneliness is negatively related to instant messenger use six months later in adolescents.

evidence.description: A 2-wave longitudinal survey of 663 students showed instant messenger use was positively related to compulsive Internet use 6 months later.
A 2-wave longitudinal survey of 663 students showed chatting in chat rooms was positively related to compulsive Internet use 6 months later.
Instant messenger use was positively associated with depression 6 months later in a sample of 663 adolescents.
Loneliness was negatively related to instant messenger use 6 months later across the 2-wave longitudinal sample.

methodologies.name: 2-wave longitudinal questionnaire survey
methodologies.description: A 2-wave longitudinal classroom questionnaire study with a 6-month interval evaluating online communication and psychosocial outcomes in adolescents.
